title: What is the Resource Curse? Why Some of the World's Richest Countries Stay Poor
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: a valuable material or asset that can be used to produce wealth or meet people’s needs, such as oil, water, or minerals.
an established organisation or system, such as courts, elections, or government departments, that helps a society function.
to develop a wider variety of industries or activities instead of relying on just one.
excessive reliance on a single industry, product, or source of income.
the tendency of prices to change rapidly and unpredictably.
the dishonest or illegal use of power for personal gain.
wealth, success, and a high standard of living.

sentences.en: Scientists have just discovered enormous deposits of gold, diamonds, copper, or the rare earth minerals that are in smartphones and electric cars beneath your country.
sentences.zh: 科学家们刚刚在你们国家地下发现了巨额的黄金、钻石、铜，或是智能手机和电动汽车所需的稀土矿产。

sentences.en: Is this good news? Not necessarily. You might think that becoming “resource rich” is a great way for a country to become prosperous, but this not always the case.
sentences.zh: 这是个好消息吗？未必。你可能会觉得“资源丰富”是一个国家走向繁荣的绝佳途径，但事实并非总是如此。

sentences.en: Some of the world’s most resource-rich countries have struggled with corruption, dictatorship, economic instability, civil war, and widespread poverty.
sentences.zh: 世界上一些资源最丰富的国家却一直在与腐败、独裁、经济动荡、内战和普遍的贫困作斗争。

sentences.en: Instead of becoming wealthy, they have become trapped in a cycle of dependence and political turmoil.Economists have a name for this paradox: the Resource Curse.
sentences.zh: 它们非但没有变得富有，反而陷入了依赖与政治动荡的循环之中。经济学家给这种悖论起了一个名字：资源诅咒。

sentences.en: Today, we’re going to explore the resource curse.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨资源诅咒。

sentences.en: We’ll discuss why having valuable natural resources can sometimes become a disadvantage and look at some of the world’s best-known examples.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论为什么拥有宝贵的自然资源有时会成为一种劣势，并看一看世界上一些最著名的例子。

sentences.en: And we’ll do this while practicing your English listening comprehension and learning some new vocabulary!
sentences.zh: 我们将在练习英语听力理解和学习一些新词汇的同时，来完成这一切！

sentences.en: If two countries existed side by side, and one discovered enormous reserves of oil, gold, or other valuable minerals, while the other country discovered nothing at all, which country would you expect to become richer?
sentences.zh: 如果存在两个相邻的国家，其中一个发现了巨额的石油、黄金或其他宝贵矿藏的储量，而另一个国家什么也没发现，你预计哪个国家会变得更富有？

sentences.en: Most people would probably choose the country with the new natural resources.
sentences.zh: 大多数人可能会选择拥有新自然资源的国家。

sentences.en: Valuable resources can be sold to other countries.
sentences.zh: 宝贵的资源可以出售给其他国家。

sentences.en: This creates jobs, brings money into the economy, and more tax revenue for the government.
sentences.zh: 这创造了就业机会，为经济带来了资金，并为政府带来了更多税收。

sentences.en: In theory, this wealth can then be invested to improve the country and eventually spread to normal people.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，这笔财富随后可以用来投资改善国家，并最终惠及普通人。

sentences.en: The problem, though, is that this doesn’t always happen.
sentences.zh: 然而，问题在于，这种情况并非总是发生。

sentences.en: Many countries with abundant natural resources, that is countries with large quantities of valuable materials found naturally in the Earth, do not become wealthy.
sentences.zh: 许多自然资源丰富的国家，也就是地球上自然蕴藏着大量宝贵物质的国家，并没有变得富有。

sentences.en: Or, at least, do not become wealthier than other countries.
sentences.zh: 或者至少，没有变得比其他国家更富有。

sentences.en: In fact, many grow more slowly. They have maybe more political instability and could remain poorer than countries with fewer natural resources.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多国家的增长反而更加缓慢。它们的政治动荡可能更多，而且可能比自然资源较少的国家还要贫困。

sentences.en: This is known as the resource curse, or you might hear it called the paradox of plenty.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的资源诅咒，或者你可能会听到它被称为“丰饶的悖论”。

sentences.en: A paradox is a situation that seems to contradict common sense.
sentences.zh: 悖论是指一种似乎与常识相矛盾的情况。

sentences.en: In this case, the paradox is that having more valuable resources can sometimes lead to worse economic and political outcomes.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，悖论就是拥有更多宝贵的资源有时会导致更糟糕的经济和政治结果。

sentences.en: Natural resources are materials that occur naturally and can be removed from the ground and then sold.
sentences.zh: 自然资源是自然产生、可以从地下开采并随后出售的物质。

sentences.en: These include resources such as oil, natural gas, gold, diamonds, and copper.
sentences.zh: 这些资源包括石油、天然气、黄金、钻石和铜等。

sentences.en: Today, resources like cobalt, lithium, and other rare earth minerals have become really valuable because they are essential for manufacturing things like batteries, smartphones, and electric cars.
sentences.zh: 如今，像钴、锂和其他稀土矿产这样的资源变得极其宝贵，因为它们是制造电池、智能手机和电动汽车等物品必不可少的材料。

sentences.en: You might expect countries with these resources to become wealthy and powerful, but this is not guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 你可能会期望拥有这些资源的国家变得富有而强大，但这并不是保证。

sentences.en: Many resource-rich nations have struggled with political instability, meaning their governments frequently change or they face lots of conflict.
sentences.zh: 许多资源丰富的国家一直在与政治动荡作斗争，这意味着它们的政府频繁更迭，或者面临大量的冲突。

sentences.en: Other countries with resources have become economically dependent on one single export.
sentences.zh: 其他拥有资源的国家则在经济上变得依赖单一的出口。

sentences.en: They rely almost entirely on selling one resource to earn money.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎完全依靠出售一种资源来赚钱。

sentences.en: Other countries have experienced widespread corruption, where politicians or other officials use their power to become personally rich.
sentences.zh: 其他国家则经历了普遍的腐败，政客或其他官员利用他们的权力来谋取个人私利。

sentences.en: Some places have also seen increasing inequality.
sentences.zh: 一些地方还出现了日益加剧的不平等。

sentences.en: The country’s wealth is shared very unevenly.
sentences.zh: 这个国家的财富分配非常不均。

sentences.en: Only a small number of people become extremely rich, but most people remain poor.
sentences.zh: 只有极少数人变得极其富有，但大多数人依然贫困。

sentences.en: The resource curse does not mean natural resources are inherently bad or always bad.
sentences.zh: 资源诅咒并不意味着自然资源本质上是坏的或者总是坏的。

sentences.en: There are several countries that are both resource-rich and highly prosperous.
sentences.zh: 有几个国家既资源丰富又高度繁荣。

sentences.en: Norway is perhaps the most famous example.
sentences.zh: 挪威也许是最著名的例子。

sentences.en: Australia and Canada also possess enormous quantities of valuable natural resources, but they have strong economies and stable political systems.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚和加拿大也拥有数量巨大的宝贵自然资源，但它们拥有强劲的经济和稳定的政治体系。

sentences.en: So natural resources are not always a problem.
sentences.zh: 因此，自然资源并不总是问题所在。

sentences.en: But, if there is nothing inherently wrong with natural resources, why do so many countries struggle after discovering them?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果自然资源本身并没有什么问题，为什么有这么多国家在发现资源后陷入困境呢？

sentences.en: Economists usually point to a few different reasons or factors that can lead to a resource curse.
sentences.zh: 经济学家通常会指出导致资源诅咒的几个不同原因或因素。

sentences.en: One factor is overdependence. Overdependence on one industry or one resource.
sentences.zh: 其中一个因素是过度依赖。对单一产业或单一资源的过度依赖。

sentences.en: Overdependence happens when you rely on something excessively for your survival or success.
sentences.zh: 过度依赖发生在当你过度依赖某事物来求得生存或成功时。

sentences.en: You rely on it too much. For example, if you are a country which has huge oil supplies under your ground, it can be easy to rely on oil.
sentences.zh: 你对它的依赖太过了。例如，如果你是一个地下蕴藏着巨额石油供应的国家，依赖石油是很容易做到的。

sentences.en: You can earn billions of dollars by exporting that oil around the world.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过向世界各地出口石油来赚取数十亿美元。

sentences.en: More and more people in your country can get jobs working in the oil industry or related industries.
sentences.zh: 你国家里越来越多的人可以在石油行业或相关行业找到工作。

sentences.en: If oil is the most successful part of your economy, it’s easy to just focus on oil.
sentences.zh: 如果石油是你经济中最成功的部分，那么专注于石油就太容易了。

sentences.en: If oil is making so much money, why invest in anything else?
sentences.zh: 如果石油能赚这么多钱，为什么还要投资其他东西呢？

sentences.en: Why invest in manufacturing, technology, agriculture, or tourism?
sentences.zh: 为什么要投资制造业、技术、农业或旅游业？

sentences.en: Oil is much more profitable. But what happens if the oil price suddenly falls?
sentences.zh: 石油的利润要高得多。但是，如果油价突然下跌会发生什么？

sentences.en: Or if another country starts producing more oil?
sentences.zh: 或者如果另一个国家开始生产更多的石油？

sentences.en: Or if the world gradually switches to renewable energy?
sentences.zh: 或者如果世界逐渐转向可再生能源？

sentences.en: Or there is an international crisis like COVID that stops exports?
sentences.zh: 或者出现像新冠疫情这样阻止出口的国际危机？

sentences.en: A country that depends on just one industry or one resource has very few alternatives.
sentences.zh: 一个依赖单一产业或单一资源的国家几乎没有其他选择。

sentences.en: Its economy is very vulnerable because almost everything depends on the success of a single product.
sentences.zh: 它的经济非常脆弱，因为几乎一切都取决于单一产品的成功。

sentences.en: By contrast, countries with diversified economies, economies that produce many different goods and services, are much more resilient, much stronger.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，经济多元化的国家——即生产许多不同商品和服务的经济体——要坚韧得多，强大得多。

sentences.en: If one industry struggles, that’s okay, because other industries can continue growing.
sentences.zh: 如果一个行业陷入困境，那没关系，因为其他行业可以继续增长。

sentences.en: The prices of natural resources are often unpredictable.
sentences.zh: 自然资源的往往是不可预测的。

sentences.en: Economists describe this as price volatility.
sentences.zh: 经济学家将其描述为价格波动性。

sentences.en: Volatility means prices change quickly and occasionally change dramatically.
sentences.zh: 波动性意味着价格变化迅速，有时甚至发生巨大变化。

sentences.en: One year, resource prices might be very high because global demand is strong.
sentences.zh: 有一年，由于全球需求强劲，资源价格可能会非常高。

sentences.en: When the price is high, the government gets lots of high tax revenues.
sentences.zh: 当价格高时，政府会获得大量的税收收入。

sentences.en: They can afford maybe an expensive social program, or they can afford to build a new bridge.
sentences.zh: 他们或许负担得起昂贵的社会项目，或者负担得起建造一座新桥。

sentences.en: But next year, the demand for that resource falls.
sentences.zh: 但第二年，对该资源的需求下降了。

sentences.en: Or perhaps the supply increases in another country, which causes prices to fall.
sentences.zh: 或者也许另一个国家的供应增加了，这导致价格下跌。

sentences.en: This means the government income is going to fall as well.
sentences.zh: 这意味着政府的收入也将下降。

sentences.en: Maybe they can no longer afford those programs or infrastructure projects.
sentences.zh: 也许他们再也负担不起那些项目或基础设施建设了。

sentences.en: And if this happens year after year, eventually the government will fall into a lot of debt, have a lot of unfinished bridges, unfinished social programs, and generally be struggling.
sentences.zh: 如果这种情况年复一年地发生，最终政府将陷入巨额债务，拥有大量未完工的桥梁、未完成的社会项目，并且总体上面临困境。

sentences.en: Natural resources also affect politics. In many countries, governments get most of their money by collecting taxes from citizens and businesses.
sentences.zh: 自然资源也会影响政治。在许多国家，政府的大部分资金是通过向公民和企业征税来获得的。

sentences.en: Because people pay taxes, they expect the government to spend their money responsibly.
sentences.zh: 因为人们缴纳了税款，他们期望政府负责任地花钱。

sentences.en: Spend it on hospitals or schools or roads.
sentences.zh: 把钱花在医院、学校或道路上。

sentences.en: But in resource-rich countries, things are sometimes a bit different.
sentences.zh: 但在资源丰富的国家，情况有时会有些不同。

sentences.en: It has been argued that governments are less accountable.
sentences.zh: 有人认为，政府的问责度较低。

sentences.en: They rely less on taxpayers. The government maybe doesn’t need your income taxes because they own all the oil and all the metals under the ground, and they make their money by selling oil and metal.
sentences.zh: 它们对纳税人的依赖较少。政府可能不需要你的所得税，因为它们拥有地下的所有石油和所有金属，它们通过出售石油和金属来赚钱。

sentences.en: But because you’re not paying taxes, because the government doesn’t rely on you, they don’t need to listen to you as much.
sentences.zh: 但因为你没有纳税，因为政府不依赖你，它们就不需要那么多地倾听你的意见。

sentences.en: This creates a lot of opportunities for corruption.
sentences.zh: 这为腐败创造了大量的机会。

sentences.en: Corruption is the dishonest use of power for personal benefit.
sentences.zh: 腐败是为了个人利益而不诚实地使用权力。

sentences.en: There are many types of corruption. Politicians might award a mining contract to their friend or family members.
sentences.zh: 腐败有多种类型。政客可能会将采矿合同授予他们的朋友或家庭成员。

sentences.en: Politicians might accept a bribe from companies hoping to gain access to valuable resources.
sentences.zh: 政客可能会接受希望获得宝贵资源准入的公司的贿赂。

sentences.en: Perhaps money that is supposed to be spent on schools might instead disappear into a private bank account in another country across the world.
sentences.zh: 也许本该用于学校的资金反而消失在世界另一个国家的私人银行账户中。

sentences.en: And of course, as you all know, natural resources often contribute to conflict.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如大家所知，自然资源往往会引发冲突。

sentences.en: Different groups compete for control of resources because power and money comes from resources.
sentences.zh: 不同的群体争夺对资源的控制权，因为权力和金钱来自于资源。

sentences.en: There are so many examples of this and of these competitions becoming violent.
sentences.zh: 这方面的例子不胜枚举，这些竞争演变成暴力冲突的例子也屡见不鲜。

sentences.en: Natural resources don’t automatically cause wars or dictatorships, but they can make existing conflicts more intense or perhaps more likely to become violent.
sentences.zh: 自然资源不会自动引发战争或独裁统治，但它们会使现有的冲突更加激烈，或者可能更容易演变成暴力冲突。

sentences.en: One of the most famous examples of a country suffering from a resource curse is the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the DRC.
sentences.zh: 遭受资源诅咒最著名的国家之一是刚果民主共和国，即刚果（金）。

sentences.en: The DRC is perhaps not the best example of a resource-cursed country, but it is a very clear example.
sentences.zh: 刚果（金）也许不是资源受诅咒国家的最佳例子，但它是一个非常清晰的例子。

sentences.en: It is located in Central Africa, and it is one of the largest countries on the continent, actually, in the entire world.
sentences.zh: 它位于中非，实际上是该大陆、乃至整个世界上面积最大的国家之一。

sentences.en: The DRC is also perhaps the most resource-rich country on the planet, definitely one of the most resource-rich countries on the planet.
sentences.zh: 刚果（金）也许也是地球上资源最丰富的国家，绝对是地球上资源最丰富的国家之一。

sentences.en: Beneath the DRC lies enormous deposits of copper, cobalt, gold, diamonds, tin, and coltan.
sentences.zh: 刚果（金）地下蕴藏着巨额的铜、钴、黄金、钻石、锡和钶钽铁矿储量。

sentences.en: Coltan is particularly important because it contains the metals we need to make smartphones, laptops, and other electric devices.
sentences.zh: 钶钽铁矿尤为重要，因为它包含我们制造智能手机、笔记本电脑和其他电子设备所需的金属。

sentences.en: The DRC is especially famous for its cobalt reserves.
sentences.zh: 刚果（金）以其钴储量而闻名。

sentences.en: Cobalt is the metal that is used in rechargeable batteries, including those that are in electric cars.
sentences.zh: 钴是用于可充电电池的金属，包括电动汽车中的电池。

sentences.en: The DRC, produces around two-thirds, 66%, of the world’s cobalt, making it the most important supplier of cobalt in the world.
sentences.zh: 刚果（金）生产了全球约三分之二（即66%）的钴，使其成为世界上最重要的钴供应商。

sentences.en: If you look at these facts, the fact the DRC has copper, cobalt, gold, coltan, diamonds, tin, all of these different metals, you might expect the DRC to be one of the wealthiest countries in Africa.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一下这些事实，即刚果（金）拥有铜、钴、黄金、钶钽铁矿、钻石、锡以及所有这些不同的金属，你可能会期望刚果（金）成为非洲最富有的国家之一。

sentences.en: But it is one of the poorest. Despite its extraordinary natural wealth, millions of people in the country live in poverty.
sentences.zh: 但它是最贫穷的国家之一。尽管拥有非凡的自然财富，该国仍有数百万人生活在贫困之中。

sentences.en: Large parts of the DRC have experienced decades of violence and political instability.
sentences.zh: 刚果（金）的大片地区经历了数十年的暴力和政治动荡。

sentences.en: The resource curse alone can’t explain the problems with the DRC.
sentences.zh: 单靠资源诅咒无法解释刚果（金）的问题。

sentences.en: During the late 19th century, the territory became the personal possession of King Leopold II of Belgium.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪后期，这片领土成为了比利时国王利奥波德二世的私人领地。

sentences.en: Under his rule, the local population was brutally treated and they were forced to extract the resources, especially rubber and ivory, and then send these resources out of the DRC.
sentences.zh: 在他的统治下，当地居民受到残酷对待，他们被迫开采资源（尤其是橡胶和象牙），然后将这些资源运出刚果（金）。

sentences.en: Millions of Congolese people suffered from forced labor and violence.
sentences.zh: 数百万刚果人民遭受了强迫劳动和暴力的折磨。

sentences.en: When the DRC became independent in 1960, it inherited weak institutions.
sentences.zh: 当刚果（金）于1960年独立时，它继承了脆弱的机构。

sentences.en: Institutions are the organizations and systems that help a country function: courts, government departments, the legal system.
sentences.zh: 机构是指帮助国家运转的组织和系统：法院、政府部门、法律体系。

sentences.en: Building strong institutions takes time, and the DRC didn’t have them.
sentences.zh: 建立强大的机构需要时间，而刚果（金）没有这些。

sentences.en: Belgium never built strong institutions.
sentences.zh: 比利时从未建立起强大的机构。

sentences.en: The country faced political crisis almost immediately.
sentences.zh: 这个国家几乎立刻就面临了政治危机。

sentences.en: The DRC has experienced dictatorships, corruption, foreign intervention, and wars.
sentences.zh: 刚果（金）经历了独裁统治、腐败、外国干涉和战争。

sentences.en: There’s been a lot of armed conflict over mining areas because the valuable resources in mines can be sold to buy weapons and finance their military operations.
sentences.zh: 围绕采矿区发生了大量武装冲突，因为矿山中的宝贵资源可以出售来购买武器并为其军事行动提供资金。

sentences.en: Today, the situation in the DRC is really complex.
sentences.zh: 今天，刚果（金）的局势非常复杂。

sentences.en: The world’s growing demand for electric vehicles and rechargeable batteries has made cobalt and copper super valuable.
sentences.zh: 世界对电动汽车和可充电电池不断增长的需求使得钴和铜变得超级宝贵。

sentences.en: This creates opportunities for the DRC, but also competition over who controls these resources and who benefits from their sale.
sentences.zh: 这为刚果（金）创造了机遇，但也引发了关于谁控制这些资源以及谁从其销售中受益的竞争。

sentences.en: The DRC’s extraordinary mineral wealth, has made its problems far more difficult to solve.
sentences.zh: 刚果（金）非凡的矿产财富使其问题变得更加难以解决。

sentences.en: It has been cursed by its resources. Countries on several different continents have experienced similar problems.
sentences.zh: 它被其资源所诅咒。几个不同大陆的国家都经历过类似的问题。

sentences.en: Nigeria is Africa’s most populous country, the country with the biggest population, and also one of Africa’s largest oil producers.
sentences.zh: 尼日利亚是非洲人口最多的国家，人口规模最大的国家，也是非洲最大的产油国之一。

sentences.en: Oil was first discovered in large quantities in the 1950s, and now oil is a really large share of Nigeria’s export earnings and government revenue.
sentences.zh: 石油在20世纪50年代首次被大规模发现，现在石油占尼日利亚出口收入和政府收入的很大一部分。

sentences.en: But Nigeria has struggled to convert oil wealth into economic prosperity.
sentences.zh: 但尼日利亚一直在努力将石油财富转化为经济繁荣。

sentences.en: Because oil has been so profitable, other industries, especially manufacturing, have received less investment.
sentences.zh: 因为石油利润丰厚，其他行业（尤其是制造业）获得的投资较少。

sentences.en: People invest in oil, so they don’t invest in manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 人们投资石油，所以他们不投资制造业。

sentences.en: This has made Nigeria’s economy vulnerable when oil prices fall.
sentences.zh: 这使得尼日利亚的经济在油价下跌时变得脆弱。

sentences.en: Nigeria also faces serious problems with corruption.
sentences.zh: 尼日利亚还面临着严重的腐败问题。

sentences.en: Quite often in the news, you will see stories of billions of dollars in oil revenue disappearing through fraud or illegal activities.
sentences.zh: 你经常会在新闻中看到数十亿美元的石油收入通过欺诈或非法活动消失的故事。

sentences.en: Some parts of Nigeria have benefited greatly from oil production, some people as well, but most ordinary Nigerians haven’t seen as much improvement in their daily lives as you would expect.
sentences.zh: 尼日利亚的一些地区从石油生产中受益匪浅，一些人也是如此，但大多数普通尼日利亚人并没有看到他们的日常生活有你所期望的那么多改善。

sentences.en: Furthermore, oil is a damaging natural resource.
sentences.zh: 此外，石油是一种破坏性很强的自然资源。

sentences.en: It has polluted Nigeria’s rivers and farmland, making it more difficult for local people to live because their farms are now polluted.
sentences.zh: 它污染了尼日利亚的河流和农田，由于农田遭到污染，当地人民的生活变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Another example is Venezuela. Venezuela possesses some of the largest oil reserves in the world.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是委内瑞拉。委内瑞拉拥有世界上一些最大的石油储量。

sentences.en: For a long time, oil exports were a big part of the government’s income, and oil exports financed Venezuela’s really ambitious spending programs.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，石油出口是政府收入的大头，石油出口资助了委内瑞拉雄心勃勃的开支项目。

sentences.en: Venezuela, of course, is a socialist country, and they had really ambitious public spending programs.
sentences.zh: 当然，委内瑞拉是一个社会主义国家，他们有雄心勃勃的公共开支项目。

sentences.en: But the success of the oil industry created dependence.
sentences.zh: 但石油产业的成功造成了依赖。

sentences.en: When global oil prices started to fall, Venezuela’s economy entered a severe crisis.
sentences.zh: 当全球油价开始下跌时，委内瑞拉经济陷入了严重危机。

sentences.en: The government revenues collapsed and inflation reached extraordinary levels.
sentences.zh: 政府收入崩溃，通货膨胀达到了惊人的水平。

sentences.en: Of course, the resource curse is only part of this story.
sentences.zh: 当然，资源诅咒只是这个故事的一部分。

sentences.en: Political decisions, economic mismanagement, international sanctions, and many other things also contributed to Venezuela’s crisis.
sentences.zh: 政治决策、经济管理不善、国际制裁以及许多其他因素也导致了委内瑞拉的危机。

sentences.en: But the fact the country was so reliant on oil made these problems far more severe.
sentences.zh: 但该国如此严重依赖石油这一事实，使得这些问题变得更加严重。

sentences.en: Angola is again another example. Following the end of its long civil war, Angola experienced rapid growth because oil production expanded.
sentences.zh: 安哥拉又是另一个例子。在其漫长的内战结束后，随着石油产量的扩大，安哥拉经历了快速增长。

sentences.en: For a while, it was one of Africa’s fastest-growing economies.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，它是非洲增长最快的经济体之一。

sentences.en: A large amount of the government’s revenue comes from the oil sector, but that means changes in oil prices have a really big impact on Angola’s public finances.
sentences.zh: 政府的大部分收入来自石油部门，但这意味着油价的变化对安哥拉的公共财政有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: When the oil prices fall, Angola’s government spending has had to be slashed, reduced, and that has affected its public services.
sentences.zh: 当油价下跌时，安哥拉政府的开支不得不大幅削减，这影响了其公共服务。

sentences.en: Many economists argue that Angola still needs to diversify its economy by investing more in agriculture or manufacturing or other industries.
sentences.zh: 许多经济学家认为，安哥拉仍然需要通过对农业、制造业或其他行业的更多投资来实现经济多元化。

sentences.en: Not all examples involve oil. During the 1990s, Sierra Leone became internationally known for its diamond industry.
sentences.zh: 并非所有例子都涉及石油。在20世纪90年代，塞拉利昂因其钻石产业而在国际上闻名。

sentences.en: Diamonds are very valuable, but during the country’s civil war, different groups started to take control of diamond mines and then sell these diamonds illegally to buy weapons and continue fighting.
sentences.zh: 钻石非常宝贵，但在该国内战期间，不同的武装开始控制钻石矿，然后非法出售这些钻石以购买武器并继续战斗。

sentences.en: These diamonds became known as blood diamonds or conflict diamonds.
sentences.zh: 这些钻石被称为血钻或冲突钻石。

sentences.en: These were diamonds sold to finance armed conflict.
sentences.zh: 这些是为了资助武装冲突而出售的钻石。

sentences.en: So if a country discovers oil or other valuable materials, is it automatically going to become corrupt or economically dependent on that resource?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果一个国家发现了石油或其他宝贵物质，它会自动变得腐败或在经济上依赖该资源吗？

sentences.en: No. Some countries have managed their resources really well.
sentences.zh: 不会。一些国家将它们的资源管理得非常好。

sentences.en: Instead of allowing their resources to dominate their economies, they have used it to build prosperity.
sentences.zh: 它们没有让资源主导自己的经济，而是用资源来建立繁荣。

sentences.en: The country most often praised by economists is Norway.
sentences.zh: 最常受到经济学家称赞的国家是挪威。

sentences.en: In the late 1960s, large oil and gas reserves were discovered underneath the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60年代后期，人们在北海下方发现了巨大的石油和天然气储量。

sentences.en: This means that Norway is one of the largest exporters of oil and natural gas in the world.
sentences.zh: 这意味着挪威是世界上最大的石油和天然气出口国之一。

sentences.en: But unlike other oil-producing countries, Norway has avoided the resource curse.
sentences.zh: 但与其他产油国不同的是，挪威避开了资源诅咒。

sentences.en: One reason is that Norway already had really strong democratic institutions before oil was discovered.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是挪威在发现石油之前就已经拥有了非常强大的民主机构。

sentences.en: It had a stable political system, an independent legal system, low levels of corruption, high levels of public trust.
sentences.zh: 它拥有稳定的政治体系、独立的法律体系、较低的腐败水平和高度的公众信任。

sentences.en: This meant the government could manage its new wealth effectively.
sentences.zh: 这意味着政府可以有效地管理其新财富。

sentences.en: Norway created a sovereign wealth fund. A sovereign wealth fund is a government-owned investment fund.
sentences.zh: 挪威创建了一个主权财富基金。主权财富基金是政府拥有的投资基金。

sentences.en: Instead of spending all of their money earned from oil immediately, Norway invests it.
sentences.zh: 挪威没有立即花掉从石油中赚取的所有钱，而是将其投资出去。

sentences.en: They invest it in companies, property, financial markets.
sentences.zh: 他们将其投资于公司、房地产和金融市场。

sentences.en: Oil and gas will eventually run out, but by investing their profits, Norway is providing income for the future.
sentences.zh: 石油和天然气最终会枯竭，但通过投资利润，挪威正在为未来提供收入。

sentences.en: In fact, Norway’s sovereign wealth fund is the largest in the world, worth well over one trillion US dollars.
sentences.zh: 事实上，挪威的主权财富基金是世界上最大的，价值远超一万亿美元。

sentences.en: Another success story comes from Botswana.
sentences.zh: 另一个成功的故事来自博茨瓦纳。

sentences.en: When Botswana became independent from Britain in 1966, it was one of the poorest countries in the world.
sentences.zh: 1966年博茨瓦纳从英国独立时，它是世界上最贫穷的国家之一。

sentences.en: Shortly after independence, they discovered diamonds.
sentences.zh: 独立后不久，他们发现了钻石。

sentences.en: Different governments have invested their diamond revenues into infrastructure and healthcare and education.
sentences.zh: 不同的政府将钻石收入投资于基础设施、医疗保健和教育。

sentences.en: Botswana has also maintained relatively stable institutions and has kind of avoided some of the large-scale corruption you might see in places like Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 博茨瓦纳还维持了相对稳定的机构，并且某种程度上避开了你在尼日利亚等地可能看到的某些大规模腐败。

sentences.en: The country’s not perfect, of course not.
sentences.zh: 这个国家并不完美，当然不是。

sentences.en: Botswana still faces problems like inequality, but it has experienced a fast rate of economic growth, and it’s not just reliant on diamonds.
sentences.zh: 博茨瓦纳仍然面临不平等之类的问题，但它经历了经济的高速增长，而且它不只是依赖钻石。

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia has historically relied heavily on oil exports.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯历史上严重依赖石油出口。

sentences.en: Oil transformed Saudi Arabia. It funded its development and allowed the Saudi Arabian government to build massive cities and infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 石油改变了沙特阿拉伯。它资助了该国的发展，并允许沙特政府建设宏伟的城市和基础设施。

sentences.en: But Saudi Arabia realized the world was going to stop using fossil fuels eventually as they try to tackle climate change and expand renewable energy.
sentences.zh: 但沙特阿拉伯意识到，随着他们试图应对气候变化并扩大可再生能源，世界最终将停止使用化石燃料。

sentences.en: If the world stops using oil, Saudi Arabia’s economy would become vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 如果世界停止使用石油，沙特阿拉伯的经济将会变得脆弱。

sentences.en: To prepare for that possibility, the government has started to diversify its economy.
sentences.zh: 为了防范这种可能性，政府已经开始实现经济多元化。

sentences.en: It’s expanded into tourism, entertainment, finance, technology, manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 它已经拓展到旅游业、娱乐业、金融、技术和制造业。

sentences.en: Projects like NEOM, which is a futuristic planned city, and major international sporting events, the World Cup in eight years’ time, are part of this strategy to reduce Saudi Arabia’s dependence on oil.
sentences.zh: 诸如未来主义规划城市NEOM以及八年后的世界杯等重大国际体育赛事，都是减少沙特阿拉伯对石油依赖这一战略的一部分。

sentences.en: They also have a sovereign wealth fund like Norway, which is one of the world’s biggest investors.
sentences.zh: 他们也拥有像挪威那样的主权财富基金，这是世界上最大的投资者之一。

sentences.en: Some economists argue that the phrase resource curse is misleading.
sentences.zh: 一些经济学家认为，“资源诅咒”这个词具有误导性。

sentences.en: Oil or diamonds or copper doesn’t make a decision.
sentences.zh: 石油、钻石或铜不会做决定。

sentences.en: They don’t create corruption or weaken economies.
sentences.zh: 它们不会制造腐败或削弱经济。

sentences.en: The real issue is not natural resources.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题不是自然资源。

sentences.en: It is the institutions, the organizations, laws, systems that are in a country.
sentences.zh: 而是一个国家的机构、组织、法律和系统。

sentences.en: Things like having an independent legal system or honest elections and effective government departments or a free press.
sentences.zh: 诸如拥有独立的法律系统、诚实的选举、高效的政府部门或自由的新闻媒体之类的事情。

sentences.en: Countries with strong institutions are generally better able to manage their wealth.
sentences.zh: 拥有强大机构的国家通常能更好地管理其财富。

sentences.en: Governments can collect taxes and then invest their money and enforce laws and stop corruption from becoming widespread.
sentences.zh: 政府可以收税，然后投资资金，执行法律，并阻止腐败蔓延。

sentences.en: Countries with weak institutions struggle to manage their resources effectively.
sentences.zh: 机构薄弱的国家在有效管理资源方面举步维艰。

sentences.en: Large amounts of money can be stolen, corruption can be common, and the government might focus on the resources more than the wider economy.
sentences.zh: 巨额资金可能被盗，腐败可能司空见惯，政府可能会把注意力集中在资源上，而不是更广泛的经济上。

sentences.en: If a country already has strong institutions, resources might strengthen its economy, like Norway.
sentences.zh: 如果一个国家已经拥有强大的机构，资源可能会增强其经济，就像挪威一样。

sentences.en: But if it has weak institutions, it might make it worse.
sentences.zh: 但如果它的机构薄弱，情况可能会变得更糟。

sentences.en: History also should be important. Many countries facing the resource curse share colonialism.
sentences.zh: 历史也应该很重要。许多面临资源诅咒的国家都有着共同的殖民历史。

sentences.en: Countries like the DRC, Nigeria, and Angola, they had decades of colonial rule before becoming independent.
sentences.zh: 像刚果（金）、尼日利亚和安哥拉这样的国家，在独立之前都经历了数十年的殖民统治。

sentences.en: Colonial governments focused on taking resources rather than building local institutions.
sentences.zh: 殖民政府专注于掠夺资源，而不是建立地方机构。

sentences.en: When these countries became independent, they inherited systems designed for taking resources out of the country, not for reinvesting the money in the country.
sentences.zh: 当这些国家独立时，它们继承的系统是为了将资源运出国家而设计的，而不是为了将资金重新投资于国内。

sentences.en: This doesn’t explain everything, but it helps us understand why some countries face greater challenges from the beginning.​
sentences.zh: 这并不能解释一切，但它有助于我们理解为什么有些国家从一开始就面临更大的挑战。

sentences.en: If your country discovered trillions of dollars worth of natural resources tomorrow, would it become automatically rich?
sentences.zh: 如果你的国家明天发现了价值数万亿美元的自然资源，它会自动变得富有吗？

sentences.en: No. We’ve seen the answer is no. Natural wealth is not a curse, but it’s also not a good thing.
sentences.zh: 不。我们已经看到了答案是否定的。自然财富不是一种诅咒，但它也并非绝对是一件好事。

sentences.en: The same oil reserves that transformed Norway into one of the wealthiest countries in the world, has contributed to political challenges in many other countries.
sentences.zh: 将挪威转变为世界上最富裕国家之一的同一批油田，却在许多其他国家造成了政治挑战。

sentences.en: The same diamonds that financed Botswana’s development fueled conflict in Sierra Leone.
sentences.zh: 为博茨瓦纳发展提供资金的同一批钻石，却在塞拉利昂点燃了冲突。

sentences.en: Countries that invest their resource profits into education, strong institutions, fighting corruption, and diversifying their economies are more likely to become prosperous, to develop long-term prosperity.
sentences.zh: 将资源利润投资于教育、强大机构、打击腐败和实现经济多元化的国家，更有可能变得繁荣，实现长期繁荣。

sentences.en: Countries that don’t do this will be trapped in cycles of dependence and instability.
sentences.zh: 不这样做的国家将陷入依赖与动荡的循环之中。

sentences.en: But what do you think? If your country suddenly discovered one of the world’s largest oil fields or mineral deposits, do you think it would use that wealth wisely?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？如果你的国家突然发现了世界上最大的油田或矿藏之一，你认为它会明智地利用这笔财富吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think it would become a victim of the resource curse?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为它会成为资源诅咒的牺牲品？
